summary: Created `OS Comparison Root CA` on node1, installed it as a RHEL system trust anchor, and verified it remained trusted after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed the OpenSSL CLI from the configured RHEL repositories.
Generated a 3072-bit RSA CA key at `/etc/pki/tls/private/os-comparison-root-ca.key` with root ownership and mode 0600.
Created a self-signed CA certificate at `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/os-comparison-root-ca.crt` with CA:TRUE and certificate-signing usage.
Regenerated the RHEL system trust store with `update-ca-trust extract`.
Restarted node1 safely and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named OS Comparison Root CA
evidence.summary: Generation succeeded; direct inspection confirms the exact subject and issuer, CA:TRUE, certificate-signing usage, protected key permissions, and matching certificate/private-key public hashes.

evidence.requirement: Install the certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
evidence.summary: Trust extraction succeeded. OpenSSL default-system verification returns OK, and p11-kit reports `OS Comparison Root CA` as an authority trust anchor before and after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID e625b9a5-4242-499a-88da-9a76ecf86fe1; the native delayed reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned running with changed boot ID daf8e7ba-4cc4-48c4-9505-f3c2ed5e8ec1; post-restart checks confirm the CA files, key match, trust-anchor registration, and default-system verification recovered.
